Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Manu Khare
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sachchida Nand Ojha
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Sachchida Nand Ojha,
learned Counsel for the informant and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married on 08.12.2023 with the son of the applicant and sufficient dowry was given, however, the entire matrimonial family used to harass her for more dowry and subsequently, after about four months on 16.04.2023, an information was received from the neighbours that the daughter of the informant had died by hanging.

3. The submission of the Counsel for the applicant is that in the postmortem report, which is on record, no injury is shown and the cause of death is combined effect of asphyxia, varicose congestion Rekha Shukla vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69978120/

sentences.text: due to ante-mortem hanging and its complication.
The Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the report of the FLS, Kannauj which did not find any remains of human body.
In the light of the said, the submission of the Counsel for the applicant is that the applicant being the mother-in-law have been falsely implicated.

It is further argued that even for the sake of argument, the allegations are treated to be correct, the allegation at best would attract offence under Section 498A IPC and not under Section 304B IPC as the allegation of subjecting the deceased to cruelty 'soon before death' is missing.
It is also argued that the applicant is aged about 56 years and is in custody since 16.04.2023.

4. Learned A.G.A. and learned Counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the bail prayer and argues that the matrimonial family did not even inform the informant, which was informed by the neighbours, which demonstrates the state of mind of the entire family members and as such,
considering the fact that the daughter of the informant died within four months of marriage, the bail application is liable to be rejected.
5.

Considering the submissions made at the bar and from the perusal of the FIR, the allegations with regard to demand of dowry are levelled against the entire family members, however, there is no specific allegation against any of the family members including the applicant; prima facie, there is no allegation of harassment either physical or mental soon before the death; the medical report on record also does not indicate physical or mental cruelty soon before death; the applicant is a lady and is in custody since 16.04.2023, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Rekha Shukla be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.119 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Barra, District Kanpur Nagar on her furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
